notes.title: MISSION EDITOR MODE AVAILABLE NOW - UPDATE 1.5.0
notes.content:
Greetings Pharaohs, 

Today, we’re glad to announce that the [url=https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/1351080/manuals/Mission_Editor_Guide_EN.pdf?t=1696860281]Mission Editor mode[/url] is now available with the latest update for Pharaoh: A New Era. Starting today, you can play the Mission Editor mode and start your kingdom from scratch to rule it in your own way. 

[b][h3]Disclaimer regarding map names when playing in Mission Editor mode:[/h3][/b] 

A note on map names in the new Mission Editor Mode - all of your custom maps will be shown under the "[b]My Maps[/b]" tab in-game.

You may create additional tabs to organize your custom maps in-game by creating folders via Windows File Explorer [b](C:>Users>[My Windows User Name]>AppData>LocalLow>Triskell Interactive>Pharaoh>[Steam ID number]>My Maps)[/b].

However, please note that if you create two folders A and B, but each of them contains a map called "[b]MyMap1[/b]" then you will have two maps with the same name "[b]MyMap1[/b]" under the "[b]My Maps[/b]" tab in-game, which may lead to confusion.

We strongly encourage you to assign unique names to your custom maps to avoid confusion in the "[b]My Maps[/b]" tab.

notes.title: NEW UPDATE 1.4.0 AVAILABLE ON PHARAOH: A NEW ERA
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings Pharaohs, [/h3]

Today, we are ready to deploy a new update to Pharaoh: A New Era that addresses bug fixes and issues in the military system.

Thanks to the community feedback received since the game launched, the development team worked to address issues related to the military system alongside a new Defense System that brings new purpose to fortifications.
 
[h3][b]Added Defense System: [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] Defensive structures now trigger a defensive zone around them
[*] Surrounding a zone with defensive structures protects it entirely
[*] Civil buildings located in a defensive zone cannot be destroyed in the aftermath of a battle
[*] All invasions now trigger a round of destruction of civil buildings (can only be countered if your army is stronger than the invader’s)
[*] Your city is now more vulnerable to destruction if you lose or narrowly win a battle
[*] Added Defense Overlay to display the current defensive zones
[*] Predators inside a defensive zone can no longer attack walkers
[/list]

[h3][b]Fixed: [/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed Overseer of the Military displaying bow icon for upgraded infantry
[*] Fixed soldiers layering on battle screen
[*] Enemy death count now rounds up properly
[*] Increased tower effect on battle calculation
[*] Decreased the price for walls, towers and gatehouses 
[*] Fixed troop returns event message
[*] Temple Complex to Seth bonuses are now: Losing fewer troops during battles and Troops gain more experience after a battle
[*] The Overseer of the Military is now disabled on maps where no military building is available
[*] Overseer of the Treasury now displays money loss after being defeated in battle
[/list]

notes.title: PHARAOH: A NEW ERA - NEW PATCH 1.3.0 AVAILABLE NOW
notes.content:
Greetings Pharaohs,

We’re deploying a new update that brings several QoL improvements as well as bug fixes to Pharaoh: A New Era. As always, the team is grateful to the community for its everlasting support and love for the game.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1351080/Pharaoh_A_New_Era/

[h3][b]NEW OVERLAYS[/b][/h3]

NEW - Three more overlays added
[list]
[*] Bazar overlay - displays food access to houses
[*] Magistrate overlay - displays courthouses access to houses
[*] Problems - displays various problems in your city : 
[*]Risk of life, collapse, crime, disease, and malaria
[*] No road access
[*] Buildings’ entry & exits that are not connected
[*] No access to the workforce
[*] No raw material available for manufactured goods production buildings
[*] No resources available for services buildings (i.e. mortuaries, scribal schools, libraries, senet houses, and zoos)
[*] Entertainers missing on performance venues
[/list]
Most overlays now display information when you hover on the buildings. Furthermore, we added an option to display columns on overlays just like in the original game

[h3][b]EVENT MANAGEMENT[/b][/h3]

With this new update, you can now manage which events must be displayed as a notification or should be hidden. This setting can be used in a new tab in the ‘option’ menu.
Please note that [b]requests, gifts, or invasions cannot be hidden nor displayed as notifications.[/b]

We also added a few new events :
[list]
[*] Population milestone
[*] Warning for the lack of a working dock when a water trade route is open
[/list]

[h3][b]FLAT MODE IMPROVEMENT[/b][/h3]

Flat mode just got better with this new QoL update. Starting today, you can flatten any building with a right-click. If you right-click again the building comes up. To return to a normal view, you just have to click on the button next to the minimap or press ‘[b]F[/b]’ ([i]hotkey set by default[/i]).

The flat mode can now cover a good part of the needs related to map rotation. With this new addition, we believe that the mode will be more practical to use.

[h3][b]BURIAL GOODS[/b][/h3]

The burial goods needed are now displayed :
[list]
[*] In missions’ objectives
[*] In rating overseer
[*] In the information panel of monuments that requires them
[/list]

[h3][b]FERRIES[/b][/h3]

While fixing bugs that affected ferries, something interesting occurred and we decided to keep in-game. Before, if the path of different pairs of ferries crossed, they’d stop working. After fixing this, we figured out that[b] walkers are now able to shortcut their way to go straight to a ferry landing[/b] even if it’s not the one connected to their departure.

We think that it's a neat addition, especially for bigger cities where distance can be a problem. Anything that allows path optimization is more than welcome.

[h3][b]SLEEP MODE[/b][/h3]

You can now put to sleep mode all interactive buildings. [b]Sleep mode is enabled by clicking on the Zzz button[/b] displayed in the building user interface. If you don’t want to shut down the entire industry but put to sleep mode a few buildings when lacking workers or temporarily over/underproducing certain resources, you have now a great tool to do it.

[h3][b]LEVEL DESIGN & MISSIONS EVENTS[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] In Pyramid Scheme, the first request for Granite now triggers properly
[*] In Pyramid Scheme, the trade route to Dunqul Oasis now sells and buys the proper resources
[*] Fixed soft lock occurring in Timna (Campaign sandbox) when responding in time to the recurring Men-Nefer request
[*] In Henen-nesw - Sauty trade route can now reopen
[*] In Henen-nesw - prevents a double event after receiving a gift
[*] In Meidum - trade with Abu is now possible
[*] In On -Saqqara trade route can now reopen
[*] In On - the Temple Complex Building to Ra is available now
[*] Swapped the entry and exit point in Gateway to Atlantis
[*] In Rowarty - Mycenae can no longer trade right from the start. The trade route opens later.
[*] In Behdet - the recurring perfect flood event is now a failed flood event
[*] In Iunet - The Temple Complex building to Bast is now available
[*] In Itjtawy - Balanced the wage down/wage up events to slow down general inflation
[*] In Maritis - Fixed the timeline. Events now happen three years sooner.
[*] In Thinis - the trade route to Men-Nefer can now reopen
[/list]

[h3][b]VARIOUS FIXES & OPTIMIZATIONS[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] Added mission-type icon in campaign view when choosing a monument or a military-focused quest
[*] Decreased clouds size
[*] Fixed several things on storage to prevent stuck resources
[*] Removed scripted event pause option
[*] Workforce priorities are now properly saved
[*] The uncapped Zoom option is now properly saved
[*] Stockpiling toggle in the Overseer of Commerce is now properly saved
[*] The industry shuts down toggle in the Overseer of Commerce is now properly saved
[*] Individual resources in gifts and requests are now properly displayed (i.e. blocks of sandstone, etc.)

notes.title: PHARAOH: A NEW ERA - NEW PATCH 1.2.0 AVAILABLE NOW
notes.content:
Greetings Pharaohs, 

Today we finally add the [b]long awaited ultra-wide support[/b] to the game. We also wanted to improve player experience by increasing coverage of buildings, making UI improvements and more bug fixes, most notably by fixing more [b]save corruption issues[/b] and [b]monuments getting stuck[/b].


[h3]Added ultra-wide support[/h3]

We could not test every variation out there, so if you encounter any problems, please provide your feedback in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1351080/discussions/1/]Technical Support forum[/url] so we can help you.


[h3]Balancing[/h3]

As the way to play the game has changed a lot in almost 24 years, neighborhoods tend to be generally more optimized than what the original team intended, generating spam of specific buildings to attain desired coverage. Coverage for buildings has been increased to reduce this:

[list]
[*] Shrine: from 300 to 400 people
[*] Temple: from 700 to 900
[*] Shrine for Patron God: from 150 to 200
[*] Temple for Patron God: From 375 to 450
[*] Temple Complex: from 8000 to 10000
[*] Juggler stage: from 400 to 600
[*] Musician stage: from 700 to 1000
[*] Dancer stage: from 1200 to 1800
[*] Senet House: from 5000 to 7500
[*] Zoo: from 7500 to 10000
[*] Library: from 800 to 1200
[*] Scribal School: from 300 to 500 children
[/list]


[h3]UI&UX improvement[/h3]

[list]
[*] Esc. now has the same effect as a right click.
[*] Every tooltip now gives information on what key bind is associated with its button.
[*] Added an icon on a building not having access to a road instead of a notification.
[*] Added an icon on a building whose entry and exit point are not connected.
[*] Mission briefing properly displays objectives in the first 4 missions.
[*] Objectives now display house full name instead of house level.
[/list]

[h3]General Bugfix[/h3]

[list]
[*] Trade Boats don’t get stuck when something happens to their destination dock anymore.
[*] Fixed Trade Boats not splitting when multiple docks are available.
[*] Fixed display for unit-based resources in trade boats interface.
[*] Walkers in destination mode no longer try to go through underwater floodplains (and drown on the way).
[*] Fixed some animations on buildings.
[*] Buildings destroyed by gods now have a lightning strike effect if you happen to be looking at the right time in the right place.
[*] Fixed several more cases of saves corruption.
[*] Fixed monuments getting stuck after loading a save.
[*] Fixed several other instances of monument construction getting stuck.
[*] Added burial tomb background in monument overseer.
[*] Fixed mini map not updating on certain cases.
[*] Fixed Academy blocking recruiters if not accessible by road when built the first time.
[*] Fixed tax input field not clamping the value correctly.
[*] Fixed trade routes opening and festival launching still sometimes not being able to be used while in debt.
[*] Fixed hunting lodge icon on worker overseer.
[*] Fixed workforce calculation for the overseer of workers.
[*] Disabling industries now send the workers back to being unemployed.
[*] Inhabitants in manors are now properly removed from the workforce.
[*] Fixed events on Itjtawy so new trade routes can open.
[*] Fixed "Organized Mess" achievement not being triggered.
[*] Fixed trade "Sells" column missing its border.
[*] Fixed city name not being updated when changing language in the settings.
[/list]

Please note that in order to fix as many save corruption issues as fast as possible, we were forced to reintroduce the following bugs : 
[list]
[*] When loading the campaign map, improper cities are initially being shown
[*] Work Camps will sometimes decide to stop sending out workers | WORKAROUND : This issue occurs after around 1 hour of gameplay. Reloading the save fixes the issue.
[/list]
We apologize for this inconvience, we are working to fix these bugs as fast as possible.

We want to thank you all for playing Pharaoh: A New Era. Feel free to share your feedback using Steam's [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1351080/discussions/2/]Feedback & Suggestion[/url] subforum. We're doing our best to gather everything and study them carefully. 

As stated in a dev [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1351080/view/3648515960079410286]blogpost[/url], the map editor, and military revamp are next on the list of features to come.

notes.title: PHARAOH: A NEW ERA – NEW PATCH 1.1.0 AVAILABLE NOW!
notes.content:
Greetings, Pharaohs. 

We deployed a new patch addressing some gameplay bug fixes as well as adding the highly-requested mini-map, balancing, some rework, and improvements to Pharaoh: A New Era. 

[h3][b]New Features:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Added mini-map to the bottom left of the screen.
[*]Added '[b]Flat Mode[/b]' and '[b]Grid[/b]' Toggle to the mini-map. (as explained in our previous blog post, both modes already had their own key bindings: ‘F’ & ‘G’ are used by default - can be modified in the game setting)
[*]Mini-map also displays the different food available in the mission.
[/list]
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/cf08ca7288fb15b96c603a3d73847e430ed7c14c.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Balancing:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Regrowth of trees and reeds is now calculated every month based on resources gathered and no longer total resources on the map. 
[*]Reduced the spawn rate of animals making hunters less absurdly efficient. 
[*]Hunters now bring back only 10 units of hides per trip, slowing down hides production.
[*]Reduced the rate of criminal spawn - when a house generates a criminal, the crime risk of every other house is slightly reduced, avoiding waves of criminals spawning the same day and giving you time to set up police stations and courthouses.
[/list]

[h3][b]Rework of the City Sentiment:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Added passive bonus to city sentiment each month depending on the difficulty level (+2 on easy, + 1 on normal, and no bonus on hard)
[*]If you’re supposed to get a bonus in city sentiment this month, the bonus is doubled if the city sentiment is lower than 50% and tripled if lower than 30% - allows recovering more quickly from low city sentiment once you’ve fixed the underlying problems.
[*]Added an alert if your city sentiment falls below certain thresholds - Below 50% immigration starts to decrease, and it stops below 30%).
[*]Added more information regarding the city sentiment and how variables are considered in the in-game help section
[*]Added more indications to the Chief Overseer when hovering over it - gives more precision as to why the city sentiment is falling
[/list]

[h3][b]Rework of Religion:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Festival now gives fewer ankhs to the dedicated god (from + 3 to +2 for the Grand Festival, +2 to +1 for the lavish festival, and from +1 to nothing for the small festival).
[*]The window for blessings after a festival is halved (16 instead of 32 months).
[*]Festival to a god only allows for a chance to get his blessing, not other gods anymore.
[*]General probability of getting ankhs/thunderbolts is lowered.
[*]The threshold for blessings can only be reached after you have at least dedicated a festival to the appropriate god - preventing high mood in the early game to provide free blessings.
[*]There is now a minimum delay of a month in between two blessings/wraths from different gods.
[*]The same god cannot give a blessing/trigger its wrath less than 3 months apart.
[*]You can open a trade route and throw a festival now even if you're close to going into debt. 
[*]You can open a trade route and throw a festival now when if you're in debt
[*]Tax rate cannot go higher than 25% any longer
[*]Removed every mention of the tribute to the kingdom as it’s not used in A New Era - Instead, every year passing while indebted will hurt your Kingdom Rating directly.
[/list]
 
[h3][b]UI & UX[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Key binds for overseers and overlays now close what they open.
[*]Modified the order of the overseers - reflect more what was in the original game.
[*]There are no longer subcategories to the building bar, to avoid confusion with buildings that didn’t have one - Every building is now only two clicks away.
[*]The chief overseer comments now have tooltips on hover which give more information.
[*]Saves are now ordered from newest to oldest.
[/list]

[b]Added key bindings for[/b]
[list]
[*]Undo
[*]Remove
[*]Housing
[*]Road
[*]Roadblock
[/list]
 
[h3][b]Tutorials:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Added a tutorial in Perwadjyt to explain how entertainment coverage works.
[*]Added a tutorial in Thinis to explain how flat mode works.
[*]Added a tutorial in Saqqara to explain how burial provisions work.
[*]Added a tutorial in Men-Nefer to explain how city sentiment works.
[*]Added a tutorial in Nekhen to explain how the building picker works.
[*]Modified the tutorial on Nubt to reflect the removal of subcategories.
[*]Added new loading tips.
[/list]
 
[h3][b]Options:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Added an option to toggle on/off the autosave.
[*]Added an option to specify how many autosaves to keep for a city.
[*]The autosave delay option now offers more choices.
[*]Separated the options for “[b]storage accept[/b]” into “[b]Storage Yards accept[/b]” and “[b]Granaries accept[/b]”.
[*]Added an option for unlimited zoom out (can severely hurt performance, so [b]toggle off by default[/b])
[*]The delay on hover on buildings option now offers more choices (from 0 to 3 with increments of 0.5).
[*]Remove the option for subcategories pre-open.
[/list]
 
[h3][b]Bug fixes:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]You no longer lose debens when placing a road over an existing road.
[*]Fisheries no longer stop working after a while - the boat can go back to fishing as soon as the carrier has left the building.
[*]Fixed miscalculated housing level effect on city sentiment.
[*]Victory now properly triggers its audio track.
[*]Fixed missing check on monument target if it has a worker already or not.
[*]Building a carpenter’s guild and providing it with wood after the pyramid tries to call for a carpenter no longer blocks construction.
[*]If the game is saved/loaded while Stonemasons are working on a pyramid's causeway, it will no longer block the construction.
[*]Fixed a corrupted monument sprite.
[*]Placing a bridge after removing a monument no longer breaks pathfinding.
[*]Hunting lodges now have two carriers on maps where antelopes are present to be able to deliver game meat and hide at the same time.
[*]Carriers no longer stack infinitely in certain cases.
[*]Carriers now properly remove hides from Hunting Lodges when delivering them, no longer causing over-production.
[*]Pressing UI buttons now triggers the proper sound effect.
[*]Devolving houses no longer artificially increase the number of children in the city.
[*]Fixed children count on reload.
[*]Fixed the house info close button.
[*]Fixed Architect’s Post believes it lacks workers when it has all of them.
[*]Fixed Merchants not drowning when crossing flooded areas.
[*]Prevent the building of more than 6 forts through the Building Picker.
[*]Recruiters will now produce soldiers even if an Academy is built without an initial adjacent road.
[*]Sandbox missions are now properly autosaved in French, Spanish & Italian.
[*]Fixed some cases of save corruption.
[*]Having more than 6 warships on either side no longer breaks battles.
[*]The “[i]Rends l’argent[/i]” achievement now properly unlocks.
[*]Nile farms now properly update their fertility.
[*]Numeric fields no longer let you type letters in them.
[/list]
 
[h3][b]Level Design:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Breweries are now available in Sawu.
[*]Breweries are now available in Djedu.
[*]Breweries are now available in Hetepsenusret.
[*]Breweries are now available in Baharyia Oasis.
[*]Fixed trade prices on manufactured goods in Sawu.
[*]Music is back in Itjtawy.
[*]And many more minor fixes.
[/list]
 
[h3][b]Localization:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Words like “main d‘œuvre” are now properly displayed in French.
[*]Various corrections in the 5 languages.
[*]Cities' names are now the same on the map and in the campaign choices.
[*]Fixed certain localization keys that stayed in English while playing in another language.
[*]Seth's blessing event now properly explains that only part of the attackers is killed by the god.
[*]Fixed localization lines for the altar and oracle built-in Temple Complexes.
[*]Fixed inverted descriptions for Ptah's wraths.
[/list]

Feel free to share them using the "[url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1351080/discussions/2/]Feedback & Suggestion[/url]" subforum on Steam. notes.title: PHARAOH: A NEW ERA - Q&A BEHIND THE ART (PART 2/2) 🎨
notes.content:
Greetings everyone!

Today, we are back with [b]the following (and last) part of the dev blog about the game’s Art Direction. [/b]

First of all, we would like to apologize for the delay as this dev blog was supposed to be out last month. To be honest with you all, bad luck hit us, and part of the social team in charge was on sick leave for a while.  Anyway, we are back now, and here are some more answers from [b]Guillaume (aka [url=https://twitter.com/Breizh_Noodle?s=20&t=l_LkVmzvhzbcM7ipBPq0sg]Noodle[/url]) - Art Director at Triskell Interactive![/b] I hope you’ll enjoy reading this last part of the dev blog!

[i][b]In the end, please keep in mind that every choice was made with deep respect, passion, and love for the original game.[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/35822e7452cb5c1cc4a39f0cbcf47e3e8256996c.png[/img]

[h3]💬 [b]INTERVIEW Q&A[/b][/h3]

➣ [b]The amount of work to redesign each asset must be huge, but I imagine you also have to work on some of the sprite details, which were not necessarily there before. How do you deal with that?[/b]

Since we don't have access to the original game files, we always start working on the in-game version and scale up each asset by 2000%. It gives us a good idea of what we're working on (that's also the part when we realize that some of the details of the original game are just a bunch of pixels!). Then, we have to figure out what we are dealing with and whether this bunch of pixels is more of a carpet or a jar. Sometimes, it is even difficult to distinguish the different textures. We sometimes even wonder if we are dealing with earth, mud, or brick. So, my job is to find out what these textures are, to add details like cracks in a wall or some flowers… Also, I usually "edit" the work files, either for myself or for the team. In other words: I get the original sprite, then enlarge it and identify what might be blurry (or unclear). Finally, I put references for some objects or textures, and I establish a color chart.

Then and only then can the painting process begin. We start with the general shapes, then sharpen the details while preserving the original sprite design. It's meticulous work, but it's also a lot of fun! By using this method, we are sure to respect the spirit of the OG.


➣ [b]What did you like best about remastering some assets? A favorite building/monument that you enjoyed (re)making? [/b]

I enjoyed working on the monuments — especially those of the original Cleopatra extension like the Caesareum. These are Greek and Roman-inspired buildings with lots of colonnades, statues... It's tedious to do, but it stands out from the rest of the Egyptian buildings and brings a breath of fresh air to the overall look of the game. It was a very welcome (re)creative break!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/d1d0cda12e2466a503c642e7c9b80be82c1234fa.png[/img]

➣ [b]Do you have any particular style or inspiration in mind whenever you work on Pharaoh: A New Era?[/b]

Since Pharaoh: A New Era is all about Ancient Egypt, I have inspirations and references from historical findings and archeology. I have several books at home on the subject. IMO, Ancient Egypt is fascinating, as not a month goes by without a discovery being made. This is what makes the topic so much exciting. Otherwise, the main inspiration is the original game, of course!


➣ [b]What were your biggest difficulties during this project?[/b]

The difficulties encountered are not necessarily due to the creation itself but rather to our choice to use isometric 2D. Many difficulties result from this choice and, sometimes, influence the way we work or even the way some assets are designed. Most of the time, we have to decompose the assets of a building, making sure those bits overlap perfectly. There are also sorting issues, i.e. sprites that are not visually on the same level as others. These are technical difficulties that we have to take into account when creating graphic assets. 

Another difficulty, which also results from the use of 2D, is the isometric perspective in the drawing process. It has many advantages but also disadvantages. Indeed, the isometric perspective is not realistic.  It is a perspective that has no vanishing point, and it is sometimes very tedious to reproduce shapes like spheres, curves, or cylinders with this perspective. We often have to cheat, but as long as the visual rendering is there, cheating is allowed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/ab1bd54c172720b9de741367511128d83f46b2a8.png[/img]
[i]WIP - Overseer of the Military - Placeholder text[/i]


➣ [b]On your streams, we can see that you enjoy putting little touches of humor on the buildings. Can we expect little Easter Eggs/visuals hidden in the game?[/b]

We have always done this before at Triskell Interactive. It's more of an inside joke than anything else! In the end, we are pretty serious about our games. I don't know if there will be any Easter Eggs in the end because Pharaoh is a pretty serious game, and we have to respect that too. Pharaoh is an iconic management game and we wouldn't want players to think that we took this work lightly. We'll see!


➣ [b]What are your best memories of Pharaoh? How does it impact your creations?[/b]

I don't know if this is my "best" memory, but I remember the game being extremely difficult. I couldn't understand why my entire city was suddenly on fire. Also, I didn't understand what some of the characters were doing. For me, the walkers were merely for show. So, the most vivid memory I have is the game's replayability. It was a long learning process, but it was very exciting. I was able to try out different setups in my neighborhoods, switch the buildings around, and see the direct effects of those changes. Once you know the game mechanics, you tend to make the same neighborhoods and arrange your cities in the same way. But at the very beginning, it's the discovery, the search for perfection, the budget balance. Those are my fondest memories of the OG.

How does that impact my creations? I'm not so sure. I think what we want to do is to make a more detailed game so that the game experience is constantly renewed. I like the player to be amazed, every time they have to restart a mission, even for the 5th time in a row. I am hoping to bring back the excitement from those younger days to the fans. That would be a great accomplishment.


➣ [b]Since the demo and thanks to the feedback from the community, have some things changed in your way of seeing things?[/b]

Naturally, getting constructive and interesting feedback challenges our way of seeing things and our work in general. Nevertheless, we cannot possibly change everything based on all the feedback we have received (even though we do believe that feedback will always be necessary). The Art Direction is in line with the whole game and we got a lot of positive feedback about it during the demo. Unfortunately, it is sometimes necessary to distance ourselves from criticism because it can quickly become a source of anxiety for the team and can lead us to question the work we have accomplished or even make us doubt our abilities. Still, there were some aspects of the project that we were less sure of, and this allowed us to make certain decisions.

As for the game's UI, we noticed that it turned out to be frustrating for some players during the demo. So, we decided to redesign the user interface, menus, etc., to make the game experience as smooth as possible. notes.title: ASK ANYTHING TO CHRIS BEATRICE - ANSWERS Part.1
notes.content:
Greetings everyone, 

Last week we launched our "Ask Anything to Chris Beatrice", Lead Designer on the all-time classic and original Pharaoh from 1999. 

We'd like to thank everyone for sending out questions to Chris. He really had fun reading and answering them all. As we received a lot of questions, we had to write two different news to post everyone's questions and answers. 

[b]In this first part, you will find below all questions and answers related to the following topics: [/b]

[list]
[*] Development and Gameplay 
[*] Art Direction and History 
[*] In-game features
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/88f3ef6f0a2365f9ea52fcb9a977574b603f27e5.png[/img]

[b]Dropbear <Gibletine> (Discord): [/b]

[b]Q: Do you also eventually break down and just build slums to get to the population goal on some maps? Also, how much research went into pyramid building for the game? [/b]

Chris: Some people do play that way. It’s unfortunate that sometimes there are exploits like this that players can do or things they have to do, either to win or to get through boring flat spots in the game. It takes a lot of testing and polish to smooth all of those things out. Some missions in Pharaoh take a long time! It can be very hard to playtest well enough to identify all the pacing and balance issues that might crop up. One thing you learn as a designer is players don’t automatically play the game the way you want or expect them to. 

Pyramid research: well, yeah, a ton of work went into that. Though scholars still don’t really know all the details about how the pyramids were built (can you believe the Egyptians do not seem to have recorded this anywhere?). Again, though, back in 1999 it was all books! (and I still have them… some with the sticky notes still in). The internet was fairly useless for things like this at the time.

[b]RANCOR (Discord)

Q: How long did the development take and P and QotN take? [/b]

Chris: Pharaoh took less than a year, but remember of course we were building on Caesar III. So it’s not really accurate to say Pharaoh only took that short a time. It’s not just about having the C3 “engine” (which, in those days, wasn’t really a thing), but it is about having a fun, playable game from day one, thanks to C3. There is a lot of overhead starting a game from scratch, a lot of interdependencies, and fluidity that make it hard to get the basis for the fun established.

CotN took a lot longer because we were simultaneously getting the company off the ground, dealing with Microsoft dropping us, etc. It ended up being about four years from start to finish.

[b]GloriousCraft (Discord)

Q: How was it developing and working on Pharaoh? Stressful? Fun? Did you think it would ever reach the level of success it did at its time? [/b]

Chris: Fun? Stressful? Yes! Both and a lot of other things. Exhilarating… The experience of going through a game development cycle is very special. Once you’ve done it with a bunch of other people it’s like everyone who hasn’t done it is a “civilian.” Because it pretty much demands your whole life. At least that’s how it used to be. I wrote the Pharaoh tutorial in the maternity ward the day my son was born! I ate three meals a day with the Pharaoh team for nearly a year.

And with games, it always feels like (and often is true that) the future of the company is on the line. If the game fails or doesn’t come in on time, then some people, maybe everyone, will lose their jobs. Or the parent company won’t support your next project. Or if you’re independent it’ll be harder to get funding, etc. If you have the right people (which we did) then it’s a feeling of camaraderie, mutual sacrifice, and shared risk that is hard to express. It’s the hardest you will ever work, yet it’s not like having a real job. 

I’d never designed a game before, and in a single year, I found myself as head of the studio and designer of our big title. I knew that I didn’t know what I was doing… so I made sure first and foremost not to break anything that was fun in Caesar III. That provided a very good safety net, though it was not always easy (players and some members of the team pushed for changing things that I felt would have undermined the C3 magic). 

I never thought it would be as successful as it was, no. Everything just came together right, and the marketing group at the time, particularly the European wing (in France) really got behind it. In those pre-social media days, traditional marketing mattered a lot (press events, advertising, including billboards even).

[b]Sajuuk (Discord)

Q: What was the thing you enjoyed most about developing and/or designing in Pharaoh? Did you feel that, in the process of developing Pharaoh, you wanted to make it the most in-depth and as "historically accurate" as was possible in the context of a game, and what challenges did you come across in the process of having to implement so many unique features (like the monuments and the inundation) on top of the Caesar 3 engine? [/b]

Chris: Honestly what I enjoyed most was leading the team and the company to success.  Pharaoh didn’t need a huge team, so we all knew each other really well, and were all under one roof together all the time. But it was big enough that we had separate departments and protocols for how departments would interact. The design and the game were compact enough that one person (me) would be able to tell you at any time exactly how something was supposed to work (on top of keeping really clear and accurate design specs). That streamlines the process a lot. Pharaoh was where Impressions became a machine--a bunch of separate parts working really well together. That’s what allowed us to create Zeus the following year.

Historical accuracy
Well, yeah, I love history, and the idea of doing historical research and figuring out how to translate all that coolness into a game was pretty exciting. As far as being historically accurate, we were walking a line. A game needs to be fun, first and foremost (and by “fun” we mean addictive, sorry to say). You have to want to keep playing it. Many things that were not historic supported the fun better (such as currency).

Challenges of monuments and flood
The monuments and the flooding were very demanding on the programmers. The existing engine had obviously not been developed with anything like this capability in mind. Back then there were not really game engines: a game was coded mostly from scratch to do exactly and only what was needed for that game. So we had C3 which was a great underlying structure for the city-building stuff, but not the monuments and the flooding. 

But one thing that our team shined at was working together to deliver a good end-result come hell or high water. That meant the art, programming, and design teams working together to come up with solutions for whatever challenges were put to them. I think even we were surprised at the visual impact of the result because having things of that scale (pyramids and flooding) added an entirely new visual dimension.

[b]AnubisTheDeath (Discord)

Q: What was the biggest challenge you and the team faced when developing the original Pharaoh? [/b]

Chris: Technically it was probably the flooding. Not just the visuals (using a 2d tile-based system to transform the map), but pathing. The city-building games are all about pathing (little people and vehicles moving around, trying to get where they need to) and now we’re introducing a map that is changing in real-time, with things that can travel on water or land needing to figure out where the best way to go, not get stuck, etc.

[b]Pants (Discord)

Q: With Pharaoh, how did you and the team balance historical accuracy with gameplay and overall enjoyment? To extend the question. It is obvious that a large amount of research went into the game in order to make it as authentic as you could at the time. [/b]

Chris: I love history so much. I’ll take Vikings over GoT any day…
In making a historical game I look at it like a one-way street, that is, the history is there to inspire me, but not to limit me. I don’t owe anything to historical accuracy, but I try not to insult it too much. Because a game is not a documentary or a textbook. It has to be fun. Honestly, I might sometimes prefer to make purely educational products! But that’s not what Pharaoh is, so I basically mined the wealth of ancient Egypt for anything big that would inject fundamentally different gameplay, and/or small that would enrich that. If the historical reality would have altered the fundamental gameplay or made it less fun (as the currency example), then we had to ignore the historical reality. But in other areas, for example, the Egyptian language names for the cities--I just thought those were really cool, so I included them. 

The annual flooding of the Nile, plus using all the resources of your city to build these massive monuments are really great examples where unique historical factors of the setting were absolutely perfect for bringing the city-building gameplay to a bigger and better place. With the city-building games we always had this challenge of, why are you building that city? Ratings? That’s pretty unfulfilling and not really visual or visceral. But if you’re building a city to build a monument, then you have this massive, glorious thing growing like a progress bar or something, dependent on a pretty complex underlying machine you’ve made.

[b]Sorah (Discord)

Q: Is there anything in the game you’re especially proud of? Any funny memories while developing the game? [/b]

Chris: Personally, I’m proud of the tutorial/campaign. Before Pharaoh, the idea with our games was to get players playing the “real game” as quickly as possible. If the game was complex and needed time to learn, that was considered bad. But sometimes it was the reality. So there was often a kind of denial, as was the case with Caesar III. Give some basic instruction with a limited building set, then enable all the buildings, then off you go. That’s fine for some players, but a lot gets left out (me included, as I am not a great gamer).

With Pharaoh, I decided to embrace the richness of the gameplay and the wealth of buildings, by spreading out the introduction of buildings and resources over many scenarios. In fact, rather than try to get the player playing with all the buildings as soon as possible, I used the opposite approach, trying to make sure there were new things to introduce much further down the line. The result was a kind of synchronicity between the historical evolution of Egypt and the tiered nature of the building model in the game. 

[b]Raph'Link-Skywalker (Discord):

[b][*] We had 5 (main) deities in the game (Osiris, Ra, Ptah, Seth, and Bast), which in reality are among many in Egyptian mythology. Why these 5 and not more? [/b]
[*] Would you have liked to see one yourself (other than the already existing ones in Pharaoh the original)? I don’t understand this
[*] How difficult was it to develop a game with the game making tools at the time (which I would fittingly call "archaic") with such complex systems at the time of Pharaoh's release? What was the name of the game engine used back then?
[*] Would you consider that Pharaoh helped, in a way, to give people an overview of just how great the Egyptian civilization is? 
[*] Would you say it even gives an idea of what life in Ancient Egypt was like? 
[*] Being that we had this one after Caesar, then Zeus and Emperor, after which the series was discontinued, would you have liked to see another civilization covered, or would you have liked to go into a Pharaoh II project, much like Caesar? 
[*] [We're now looking roughly 20 years after you completed Pharaoh, how do you feel seeing that the enthusiasm around Pharaoh is still going very strong? (a remake, and lots of inspired, modern/indie titles?) [/b]

Chris: I am amazed that Pharaoh lives on in some small ways!

Pharaoh deities: The idea was to find a set of gods that synched up with the broad areas of gameplay. We could have had more or less, but when you get too many they run the risk of being less distinct from one another.

Game engine and development: Yeah, you’re right. The tools and tech were archaic, and our tech was behind the times even back then! But so are/were a lot of great games. The end result is all that matters, and if the gameplay is engaging you can get away with a lot.  

Making games in those days was a lot of smoke and mirror illusion. It still is, to a large degree, because you are always trying to get the most out of limited resources. It comes down to the different disciplines having to work together to solve problems. The designer says he wants such and such, the programming lead says “well, we can do this but not exactly that,” then the art lead says, “well if you can do this then we can make it work like such and such,” and so on.

Whether Pharaoh helped give people an overview of ancient Egypt… I don’t know! I think most of the world is and was already pretty interested in it, which benefitted us a lot. However, I will say, reading about the annual flooding of the Nile and how important the river was is not the same as playing a strategy game and feeling almost like your life depended on it. That was something I was really happy with it. You know, when you get into a game it feels like the most important thing in the world. I don’t think anyone who played Pharaoh is ever going to need it explained to them how vital the Nile river was to the ancient Egyptians.

The game probably doesn’t give a sense of what life was like in ancient Egypt, like, from the perspective of someone who lived it, but I think it does convey the factors affecting the development of the culture and the unique history and geography of the place.

I would definitely like to have seen other settings for the classic cb games after Pharaoh and Zeus, yeah.

Honestly, it’s a shock to see the enthusiasm around Pharaoh. The game changed my life. Before Pharaoh, I was not a game designer. Now (according to Google) that’s what I am. But, seriously, as a creator mostly what you dream about is your work living on. It’s not so much about commercial success (though the two are often related), it’s about making something that is outside of you that goes on to have its own life. 

[b]Vinorcola (Discord) [/b]

[b]Q: What was the most challenging part of the game development (Maybe including the first version of Caesar as Pharaoh has grown up over Caesar)? 
Q: Was there any part that made your team redo some work from scratch because of technical limitations or anything else? 
Q: Did you use a common algorithm (Dijkstra, A*, etc.) or did you have to make homemade algorithms for better performances? Thank you for your answers.
[/b]
Chris: I was only marginally involved in the design process of Caesar III (which was designed by David Lester and Simon Bradbury), but I was a witness to it. And fundamentally that’s where Pharaoh’s success comes from. In other words, they did the hard part.

The flooding of the Nile and the monument construction were pretty much entirely new systems, both from a design and a technical standpoint.

[b]GamerZahk (Discord)[/b]

In Caesar 3, there's what I call the 'immigration glitch' where on Very Hard only, between 200-300 population, people were automatically unhappy and moved out. This can get you stuck between 200-300 population forever until it ticks over 300 by force or chance and the city becomes happy again. 

This isn't an issue in Pharaoh but recently I tried the demo copy of Pharaoh and the immigration glitch was still there in the demo. 

[b]Q: I just want to know if this indeed was a bug that was fixed sometime between the Pharaoh demo and Pharaoh release or if it was a game design choice that was decided to be removed? As a second question, was the difficulty of the military on some maps like Qadesh tested on Very Hard? Because they're near impossible. Thank you for reading/answering! These have been questions I've been dealing with for years.
[/b]

Chris: It sure sounds like a bug that was fixed. In those days a lot of the development and testing of the game happened post demo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/13ea84f516f3e7cdcfaf7352dc2a4da49ca134e7.png[/img]

[b]Caesar ZX (Steam)

Q: Hey Chris, been playing Impressions city-building series for 24 years now. Here is my set of questions :

1. How are you and David Lester doing lately? 
2. How did you end up working with David in the 90s? 
3. Were all those marvelously exquisite 2D art assets in the games (the ones with walker mechanism) since Caesar 3 made with 3D software or hand-drawn in 2D? 
4. Was Pharaoh planned before Caesar 3's completion or after? 
5. Had Impressions ever considered any civilization other than Rome, Egypt, Greece and China back then? There are so many more questions I wanted to ask but I guess you might need a break.
[/b]
Chris: We’re both doing as well as anyone else! We had dinner a couple of years ago and David and I just rudely talked about the good old days while our spouses and kids indulged us. David is a great person who changed my life.

2. I answered an ad in a printed newspaper, for an art director at Impressions (“Impressions Software” at the time). I’d been working as a freelance game artist for only a few months. In those days there were artists and people who could use computers, but hardly anyone who did both. But I had been doing digital art for a couple of years, so I got the job. 

3. All the Pharaoh buildings were 3d pre-rendered. This was a transitional period where most developers (us included) were just starting to use 3d software to create assets but were not making actual 3d games yet. 

4. Pharaoh was officially decided upon after Caesar III, but the idea had been floating around for a while. It was the obvious choice for the successor if the setting were going to change. That was the only remaining question (another Rome, or a different setting?).

5. As you’ve noted, there is the typical handful of ancient world settings to choose from. But it was always “...but the monuments…!” On top of that, the European (French) marketing group really got behind the idea of doing Pharaoh.

[b]Arokh (Steam) 

Hi Chris! Ever since I saw the preview pictures for Pharaoh on the Pharaoh Heaven webpage, I wondered, why some of those gardens/statues and other buildings like small obelisks are not in the finished game?

Q: Is there something that you really wanted/planned to be in the game but didn't happen in the end?[/b]

Chris: These things happen when you have to make a game on a very short time scale. You have to produce promotional materials before the game is even designed. You’re designing the game while it’s being developed. There was no pre-production! Even the intro sequence was like, the animators create a bunch of scenes they think are cool then we figure out how to make an intro of it later. If I’d written the intro first then the gameplay design would have been delayed. 

I can’t think of anything I’d wanted to include that didn’t make it.

[b]LiVam (Steam)

Q: If you could go back and change anything about Pharaoh, what would it be?
Q: What challenges did you and the team face during development?
Q: What drew you to this time period?
[/b]
Chris:  I’d do a better job on combat, or not include it, or fundamentally changed its role in the game.

2. Not having enough time to iterate and try different ideas. It was just churning out design specs and making sure they were implemented, testing to make sure they worked and hoping they were fun. But we had the existing fun of C3 as a baseline or safety net, of course.

3. I think ancient Egypt is unique in the way it is a real, historical setting, that is at the same time mystical. This amazing culture is now basically gone. Their geography was strange, they built these monuments that I’m not sure we could build even today… everyone in the world knows about them.

They were not really city-planners, though. There was only one planned city (Amarna). So that was not a great fit as the Roman setting was. But it’s a good example of how ideas develop organically. The idea for the Caesar games came from the fact that the Romans basically transplanted their city templates all over Europe and other parts of the ancient world. Then that game became the inspiration for a game about building cities in order to construct monuments.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/78481eb7fe035054ae65c9338b06d7424004dddd.png[/img]

[b]Quackles (Discord) 

Q: Why did you decide to carry over the player's monuments for the multi-missions (Alexandria, # in the Valley) in Cleopatra, but not the rest of the city? It would have been great to just pick up where we left off.[/b]

Chris: Is this only a Cleopatra question? If so, I can’t answer it. I only supervised the design of Cleo but was pretty hands-off as I was designing Zeus at the time...

[b]Mccoy (Steam)

Q: Can you solve the mystery about the walker audio file pharaoh_e01.wav?
Q: Why is it not possible to build obelisks and pyramids in the same mission?[/b]

Chris: My friend, based on these questions, I suspect you remember more about some details of the game than I do. :) 

[b]Carsten Scheer (Facebook)

Q: Was there a feature, back in the days, you need to cut, because of technical limitations?[/b]

Chris: Well, that’s tough to answer. I mean, it’s a 2d game, so “smooth rotation” and “street-level view” might have been fun. Making a game, movie, anything, is always a question of doing the most you can with the resources you have. If PC’s had been more powerful, the Pharaoh graphics would have been higher res and had more frames of animation / higher frame rate. But I can’t think of anything the game needed that we weren’t able to do because of technical limitations.

notes.title: PHARAOH: A NEW ERA - FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
notes.content:
Greetings everyone, 

Today the development team decided to answer some of the most frequently asked questions about Pharaoh: A New Era (general questions, gameplay, etc.).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/4a8be1f1bd2875cf79c404a62718a8ba90fcfb76.png[/img]

[b][h2] [GENERAL QUESTIONS][/h2][/b]

[list]
[*] [b][u]Q: Who is working on Pharaoh: A New Era?[/u] [/b]

[*] A: Pharaoh: A New Era is developed by Triskell Interactive (Lethis series) and published by Dotemu (Streets of Rage 4, Windjammers 2…). 

[*] [b][u]Q: What is Pharaoh: A New Era?[/u][/b]

[*] A: Pharaoh: A New Era is a full remake of the iconic city builder called Pharaoh and released in 1999 by Impression Games and Sierra Entertainment. Pharaoh: A New Era features all-new 2D graphics with brand-new UI, improved gameplay mechanics. The main goal is to develop your city stone by stone and rule it like a true pharaoh.

[*] [b][u]Q: When will Pharaoh be available[/u]?[/b] 

[*] A: Pharaoh: A New Era will be available in 2021. 

[*] [b][u]Q: How much will it cost?[/u][/b] 

[*] A: The price isn’t set yet but we will announce it at a later date.

[*] [b][u]Q: How many languages will be supported? [/u][/b]

[*] A: We will give more detail about the list of languages supported in the future. Stay tuned!  

[*] [b][u]Q: Do you plan to release it on Mac and Linux?[/u][/b]

[*] A: Pharaoh: A New Era will be released on Windows only for the moment. Mac and Linux support may come later. 

[b][h2][GAMEPLAY QUESTIONS][/h2][/b]

[*] [b][u]Q: How many missions will be playable?[/u][/b] 

[*] A: There will be 53 playable missions packing more than 100 hours of gameplay. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Is there any new mode available?[/u][/b] 

[*] A: There will be a full map and mission editor available in-game, however, it won't be possible to use a custom mission from Pharaoh (1999) as the development team had to rewrite the code. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Will Cleopatra: Queen of the Nile expansion be available at launch?[/u][/b]

[*] A: Pharaoh: A New Era will include Cleopatra: Queen of the Nile at launch. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Can we expect a remaster version of Pharaoh's original soundtrack?[/u][/b]

[*] A: Yes, you can. Louis Godart is the Composer working on music arrangement (of the original soundtrack) on Pharaoh: A New Era.

[*] [b][u]Q: Do you plan to add in-game weekly challenges to Pharaoh: A New Era? [/u][/b]

[*] A: We are not planning to add in-game weekly challenges for the moment but it's a good idea that we can keep in mind for the future. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Compared to the original Pharaoh (1999), will there be any QoL-additions and if so, which one(s)? [/u][/b]

[*] A: Yes, it's in our plans and we will reveal them in the future so stay tuned! 

[*] [b][u]Q: Can we choose a very slow mode like the Original Pharaoh game? It made micromanagement way easier. [/u][/b]

[*] A: Yes, you can choose a slower speed and even build while pausing the game. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Is there going to be some kind of zoom in/out from the default view?[/u] [/b]

[*] A: Yes, you can zoom in and zoom out from the default view. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Will you keep the 90% "normal speed" and 100% "speed"? [/u][/b]

[*] A: We added different speeds so you can pick the one that suits you the most. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Will there be...more than 100 hours of gameplay? [/u][/b]

[*] A: 100 hours or even Infinite hours of gameplay if you take into account the 53 playable missions and the sandbox. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Will you add bigger maps?[/u] [/b]

[*] A: No, the maps won't be bigger. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Any plans to address walker mechanics and math bugs/glitches that the Original Pharaoh game has? [/u][/b]

[*] A: We rewrote the code and made sure to fix most of the bugs and glitches that came from the Original Pharaoh. We are also reworking walker mechanics and some more in-game stuff. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Will we have the ability to build more than three monuments on our map?[/u] [/b]

[*] A: We haven't decided yet but we'd like to add more than three monuments to the maps. 

[*] [b][u]Q: Will the game be able to run in 1440P?[/u][/b]

[*] A: Yes, Pharaoh: A New Era will run in 1440P.

[*] [b][u]Q: Will there be more resources and building in the game?[/u][/b]

[*] A: We will add more buildings to the game.

[*] [u][b]Q: There will be the possibility of mods in the game?[/b][/u][/list]

[*]A: There is no plan to support mods in Pharaoh: A New Era.

[h2][b][ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS][/b][/h2]

[*] [b][u]Q: Will dancing hippos be in Pharaoh: A New Era?[/u][/b]

[*] A: Of course! We love those dancing hippos!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38626053/7690e4edf8ebdf9e1c909f55ccb774f9c7a37b75.gif[/img]

[b]Any other question about Pharaoh: A New Era? Let us know in the comments and we'll do our best to answer them. [/b]
